actions.text: Accepted: encode_ir is at 0.9817, past the 1% minimum, and outputs are identical. Submitting for encode_ir.

actions.reason: b58encode now peels four groups of four base58 digits (four single-digit divmods by base**4) per loop pass instead of two. Typical 32- and 64-byte inputs need about half as many loop iterations, which cuts the interpreter overhead per pass (loop test, tuple build, list extend). Groups beyond the top of the integer are all zero digits and are removed by the existing lstrip, so the output is unchanged. Sandbox: encode_ir ratio 0.9817, outputs identical.

candidate.patch:
diff --git a/base58/__init__.py b/base58/__init__.py
--- a/base58/__init__.py
+++ b/base58/__init__.py
@@ -121,13 +121,17 @@ def b58encode(
     pairs, sq, big, zero = tables
     parts = []
     while i:
-        # Two groups of four digits per pass; a group past the top of i
+        # Four groups of four digits per pass; a group past the top of i
         # is all zero digits, which the lstrip below removes
         i, rem = divmod(i, big)
         i, rem2 = divmod(i, big)
+        i, rem3 = divmod(i, big)
+        i, rem4 = divmod(i, big)
         # rem is a small int: two operators are cheaper than a divmod call
         parts += (pairs[rem % sq], pairs[rem // sq],
-                  pairs[rem2 % sq], pairs[rem2 // sq])
+                  pairs[rem2 % sq], pairs[rem2 // sq],
+                  pairs[rem3 % sq], pairs[rem3 // sq],
+                  pairs[rem4 % sq], pairs[rem4 // sq])
     parts.reverse()
     return zero * (origlen - newlen) + b''.join(parts).lstrip(zero)

journal.text:
Does b58encode in base58/__init__.py spend most of its time on loop overhead rather than arithmetic? Devnet test agent, base58-py lineage. I replaced lines 124-130 (7 lines with 11) so each loop pass peels four groups of four base58 digits by divmod with base**4, instead of two. Groups past the top of the integer are zero digits and the existing lstrip removes them.

Sandbox evaluation, not a verdict. Guard ok, 1 file, 8 lines. Base and candidate built. Outputs identical. encode_ir went from 231681791 to 227435713, ratio 0.9817. decode_ir ratio 0.9931. check_ir rose from 188128303 to 189799821, ratio 1.0089.

I believe per-pass overhead in the encode loop is real but small. The check_ir rise is unexplained, since the encode loop change does not obviously reach it. The candidate is committed and queued for replay.

Next, read the check path to see why check_ir moved. The part I am least sure of is whether the extra zero groups cost more than they save on very short inputs.
